items.label: f02-redaction-by-key
items.front: What redactSensitiveMetadata redacts, and what it misses
items.back: It walks objects and arrays recursively and replaces the VALUE of any key matching /password|token|secret|apiKey|authorization|cookie|session/i with "[redacted]". It tests keys only: a secret inside a value like note: "my password is x" is kept, and a harmless key like tokenCount is redacted.

items.label: f01-queued-agent-flow
items.front: The queued agent-run flow, from button to result
items.back: Server action -> queueAgentRun: AgentRun status PENDING, a BackgroundJob type AGENT_RUN (QUEUED, attempts 0, maxAttempts 1) and an agent.run_queued audit, all sharing requestContextId. Worker: claimNextJob sets the job RUNNING, processAgentRunJob sets the run RUNNING, runs the registered agent, then SUCCEEDED (output, confidence, trace) or FAILED (errorMessage, rethrown so the job fails too).

items.label: f04-role-vs-resource
items.front: Role authorization versus resource authorization in this app
items.back: Role: requireCapability(user.role, capability) says the role may do the action at all. Resource: the target is loaded by id AND organizationId, assertCanAccessRecord refuses a missing or foreign record, and assertScopedTeam/User/Incident check every related id before the write. Both are needed.

items.label: f03-role-capabilities
items.front: Capabilities that surprise people in permissions.ts
items.back: Only ADMIN has ticket:delete. ENGINEERING can update but not create tickets, and holds job:retry and job:dead-letter. SUPPORT_AGENT can create and update tickets and create incidents, but cannot update incidents or retry jobs. MANAGER has no job actions. VIEWER has only audit:view.

items.prompt: Three staging warn logs share one fingerprint and say "disk usage high". What does the log agent report?

choices.text: Score 19, since repeated fingerprints add nothing to the anomaly score
Score 100, as three repeats of one fingerprint push it to the cap
Score 79, so the agent recommends opening a production incident now
Score 49 with no incident: it is under 70, with no production log

choices: Score 19, since repeated fingerprints add nothing to the anomaly score
Score 100, as three repeats of one fingerprint push it to the cap
Score 79, so the agent recommends opening a production incident now
Score 49 with no incident: it is under 70, with no production log

items.explanation: Each warn log weighs 8 x 0.8 (staging) = 6.4, so 19.2; a fingerprint seen 3 times adds 3 x 10 = 30, giving 49 after rounding. shouldCreateIncident needs score >= 70 AND a production log.

items.prompt: A MANAGER submits updateTicketAction moving an IN_PROGRESS ticket to RESOLVED. What happens?

choices.text: It succeeds; the action checks ticket:update and never calls canResolveTickets
The ticket is set to ESCALATED instead, as managers are not allowed to resolve
It is refused, since IN_PROGRESS is not allowed to move straight to RESOLVED
It throws, because canResolveTickets leaves the MANAGER role out of resolving

choices: It succeeds; the action checks ticket:update and never calls canResolveTickets
The ticket is set to ESCALATED instead, as managers are not allowed to resolve
It is refused, since IN_PROGRESS is not allowed to move straight to RESOLVED
It throws, because canResolveTickets leaves the MANAGER role out of resolving

items.explanation: MANAGER holds ticket:update (permissions.ts:28), and the action only runs requireCapability("ticket:update") plus assertTicketTransition; IN_PROGRESS -> RESOLVED is allowed. canResolveTickets is defined but nothing calls it.

items.prompt: Which status change does assertTicketTransition reject?

choices.text: NEW to CLOSED
CLOSED to IN_PROGRESS
CLOSED to CLOSED
RESOLVED to IN_PROGRESS

choices: NEW to CLOSED
CLOSED to IN_PROGRESS
CLOSED to CLOSED
RESOLVED to IN_PROGRESS

items.explanation: CLOSED maps to an empty list, so it cannot move anywhere else. RESOLVED may reopen to IN_PROGRESS, NEW may close directly, and canTransitionTicket returns true whenever from === to.

Database or performance degradation

choices: Authentication degradation

items.explanation: The signature checks are an if / else if chain, and the auth regex (auth|login|token|permission|sso) is tested first. "token" matches, so the database branch is never reached even though "timeout" and "db" appear.

items.prompt: An AGENT_RUN job, queued by queueAgentRun, fails on its first worker run. Which status does the worker give the job?

choices.text: FAILED, as attempts is still 0 while maxAttempts is 1
RETRYING, and the next worker loop will claim it again
QUEUED again, after the claim raised attempts to 1
DEAD_LETTERED: an agent job is allowed only one try

choices: FAILED, as attempts is still 0 while maxAttempts is 1
RETRYING, and the next worker loop will claim it again
QUEUED again, after the claim raised attempts to 1
DEAD_LETTERED: an agent job is allowed only one try

items.explanation: queueAgentRun creates the job with attempts 0 and maxAttempts 1, and claimNextJob does not touch attempts. On failure the worker sets attempts >= maxAttempts ? "DEAD_LETTERED" : "FAILED", and 0 >= 1 is false.

choices.text: "Do not retry until the payload or producer code is corrected."
"Retry with backoff; this class is usually safe to retry."
"Retry with exponential backoff and jitter."
"Retry once after reviewing recent worker logs."

"Retry with backoff; this class is usually safe to retry."
"Retry with exponential backoff and jitter."
"Retry once after reviewing recent worker logs."

items.explanation: The rule blocks run in order and each assigns retryRecommendation. The payload block (line 55) matches first, but the rate-limit block (line 76) also matches "429" and overwrites the recommendation, even though nonRetryableUntilFixed stays true.

choices.text: They are equal, because each run of digits is normalized to <n>
They differ, because the message text is hashed exactly and in full
They differ; only ids of 8 or more hex characters are normalized
They are equal only when both logs also carry the same request id

They differ, because the message text is hashed exactly and in full
They differ; only ids of 8 or more hex characters are normalized

items.explanation: createLogFingerprint lowercases the message, replaces 8+ hex runs with <id>, then any digit run with <n>, and hashes service:level:message. The request id is not part of the input.

choices.text: Both run it, because findFirst takes no lock on the selected row
The second throws, since updateMany fails on a row already locked
Only one update matches, so the other gets count 0, returning null
Both mark it RUNNING; the later write overwrites lockedBy only

items.explanation: The claim is a conditional updateMany whose where repeats status in [QUEUED, RETRYING]. After the first worker sets RUNNING, the second update matches nothing, claimed.count !== 1, and claimNextJob returns null.

critical, with escalationNeeded set to true by the incident link
